alerts.title: Significant weight gain and obesity on DTG-based ART
alerts.message: Guidelines state that weight gain should be discussed when starting ART regimens, as obesity is an increasing problem in HIV care, particularly among women, and proactive diet and exercise advice should be given to all patients starting or switching ART. Patient weight increased from 65 kg to 82 kg (BMI 25.6 to 32.4 kg/m²) over 18 months since switch to TLD, with waist circumference 96 cm. Weight gain may reflect DTG-associated effects, but overlaps with age-related and lifestyle factors and family history of T2DM; no lifestyle counselling is documented in the record.

evidence.recommended_action: Provide diet and exercise counselling per guidelines, monitor weight and BMI at each visit, and document the discussion of ART-associated weight gain with the patient.

alerts.title: Impaired glycaemia and rising BP on DTG with obesity
alerts.message: Guidelines recommend glucose monitoring every 3 months during the first year after transition to DTG. Patient now has fasting glucose 118 mg/dL (impaired), HbA1c 6.1% (pre-diabetic range), BP 138/88 mmHg (up from 118/74), and acanthosis nigricans, with prior baseline fasting glucose 92 mg/dL. Weight gain and insulin resistance may be linked to DTG, but obesity, family history of T2DM and lifestyle are competing non-drug explanations.

evidence.recommended_action: Repeat fasting glucose/HbA1c, screen for diabetes and hypertension, manage cardiovascular risk, and consider referral for evaluation of possible DTG-associated metabolic change in consultation with the ART programme.

alerts.title: Fatigue with weight gain: consider thyroid and metabolic causes
alerts.message: Guidelines list weight gain, fatigue and neck swelling among thyroid symptoms requiring evaluation. Patient reports increased tiredness alongside weight gain, dyslipidaemia (LDL 148 mg/dL, HDL 38 mg/dL, triglycerides 212 mg/dL), and hypertension. Fatigue may relate to obesity, metabolic syndrome, or sleep and mood factors rather than ART, and no thyroid assessment is recorded.

evidence.recommended_action: Assess for thyroid dysfunction (e.g., TSH) given weight gain and fatigue, and evaluate contributing metabolic and lifestyle factors.
